claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: Let the root-join blocks be the connected components of the complement. A vertex is universal exactly when its block is a singleton. If at least two universal vertices exist, pairing two of them covers every closed neighborhood. If none exists, every block has at least two vertices; choosing a,b in one block and c,d in another gives disjoint pairs (a,b),(c,d), with the first block covered by N[c]∩N[d] and every other block covered by N[a]∩N[b]. Thus the graph has a pairing dominating set and is equivalent to zero by Remark 9. The exact checker also validated this construction for 1,199 labeled connected nonexceptional cographs through six vertices.
claims.witness: The general pairing certificate is either one pair of universal vertices or the two cross-block pairs (a,b) and (c,d) described above.
claims.search_method: Structural proof from the complement-component decomposition, supplemented by exhaustive labeled-cograph enumeration and exact certificate validation.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: For a connected component with unique universal vertex u, a swap-coupling shows that playing u weakly dominates every other move for either player, even in an arbitrary disjoint context. Breaker taking u spoils every closed neighborhood, giving a zero position. After Maker takes u, C-u has at least two vertices and hence contains twins a,b. Applying Theorem 13 in both C with u Maker-owned and in C-u permits assigning a to Maker and b to Breaker; b spoils u, while every vertex of C-u is happy in C exactly when it is happy in C-u. Hence Maker opens the child forest and Breaker deletes the tree. Recursion gives the forward reduction. Conversely, realize a leaf by K1 and an internal node by joining a new vertex to the disjoint union of its child realizations and a zero K2 ballast. The ballast makes the new vertex uniquely universal and adds only constant size per node. Both maps preserve thresholds and the designated starter with polynomial, in fact linear-output, overhead. Exact minimax matched the reduction on all 6,039 labeled cographs through six vertices.
claims.witness: Forward witness R(G): zero components are omitted, K1 becomes a prize leaf, and each unique universal vertex becomes a root over R(C-u). Inverse witness: add a zero K2 ballast below every internal root before taking the join with its new universal vertex.
claims.search_method: Context-preserving strategy transposition, twin-pair reduction via Theorem 13, recursive construction in both directions, and exhaustive exact comparison on bounded labeled cographs.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Inductively discard zero children and let A be a prize leaf. An internal node with zero or one A-child has both starting scores zero, so Theorem 6 makes it equivalent to zero. With two A-children, Maker opening produces A+A, which is the constant-one game, whereas Breaker deletes the subtree for zero; these are exactly A's two options, so the node is equivalent to A. Thus every subtree reduces to A or zero, and a forest with z surviving A-types has scores ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2). A bottom-up cotree traversal performs constant work per node. The checker confirmed the formula on 1,351 forests assembled from all 398 rooted binary trees through ten total nodes.
claims.witness: Canonical transition: 0 or 1 surviving A-child maps to zero; exactly 2 surviving A-children map to A; a top-level multiset of z A-games maps to z isolated prize leaves.
claims.search_method: Induction on rooted-tree height using game equivalence and Theorem 6, plus exhaustive exact minimax over bounded rooted binary forests.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For a multiset S of unopened star sizes and l exposed leaves, the unrestricted minimax recurrences consider taking an exposed leaf, opening any star, or deleting any star. A simultaneous strong induction on remaining vertices proves two exchange inequalities for j≤k: replacing an unopened j-star by a k-star cannot decrease either starting value, and exposing k while retaining j is at least as favorable to Maker as exposing j while retaining k. Common-star and exposed-leaf moves preserve the induction relation; opening the distinguished stars produces equal total exposed prizes, while deleting them leaves the first position with additional exposed prizes, which cannot reduce either score by Milnor's inequalities. Therefore Breaker may delete and Maker may open a largest remaining star. Sorting leaves only prefix states M(i,l),B(i,l), yielding the displayed recurrences. There are O(rK)=O(n^2) states and constant work per state. Exact unrestricted minimax agreed on 110,110 bounded states; 166,320 replacement and 83,160 opening-exchange inequalities were also checked.
claims.witness: The dynamic-programming state is a sorted prefix of unopened star sizes together with the exposed-leaf count; the largest remaining star is the only star transition required for either player.
claims.search_method: Exact unrestricted recurrence, simultaneous monotonicity/exchange induction, state-count analysis, and exhaustive integer minimax comparison for up to six stars of size at most nine and ten initially exposed leaves.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: Exact game-tree minimax gives P3=(1,0) and K1,3=(1,0), but P3+P3=(1,1) while P3+K1,3=(2,1). Both graphs are cographs. Consequently, a union-node transition receiving only the children's standalone score pairs cannot distinguish substituting K1,3 for P3, although the correct parent value changes.
claims.witness: P3 with edges {01,12} and K1,3 with edges {01,02,03}; their respective disjoint unions with P3 have score pairs (1,1) and (2,1).
claims.search_method: Complete integer-and-bitmask minimax over every legal move for the four explicit graphs.

target_evidence: The exact target demands a full classification of SHVG on all cographs by either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness theorem. The draft proves a material exact equivalence with a rooted-forest game and polynomial algorithms for two proper subclasses, but it supplies neither an algorithm nor hardness for unrestricted rooted forests. It therefore makes valid partial progress and does not fully resolve the target. Its claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, and the final writeup explicitly says the complete classification remains unresolved, so that claim is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
